posts.caption: Patara — Lycia's once-largest city, where Saint Nicholas was born. Columns rising from sand dunes, a theatre still in use, an 18-kilometre beach where loggerhead turtles nest. This place keeps too many stories.
posts.cta: Tap save — golden hour visit at 18:30 is unforgettable.
posts.notes: Drone reveal of columns 0-8s, theatre 8-20s, beach pan 20-35s, sunset over dunes 35-45s.

posts.caption: Patara Beach at sunset. Eighteen kilometres of empty sand. The kind of horizon that makes you forget your phone.
posts.cta: Save for the perfect sundown spot.
posts.notes: Long pan + footprint close-up + horizon static end frame.

posts.caption: Xanthos — once the largest city of Lycia. The Harpy Monument, the inscribed pillar telling its own history, the burned-twice city that always rebuilt. UNESCO World Heritage, 40 minutes from Kalkan.
posts.cta: Save — best visit time is 09:00 before the heat.
posts.notes: Hero shot of Harpy tomb 0-5s, then pillar inscriptions, theatre wide, agora drone.

posts.caption: Paragliding from Babadağ — Ölüdeniz from 2000 metres. The 30 minutes before landing make a year of normal days look small.
posts.cta: Book through our partners — DM for current price.
posts.notes: Takeoff 0-5s, sky pan 5-15s, lagoon approach 15-22s, landing 22-25s.

posts.caption: Letoon — three temples for three deities, Leto, Apollo and Artemis. Reflected in a sacred pool, walked on by the Lycian League for 800 years. Twenty minutes from Kalkan.
posts.cta: Save — combine with Xanthos for a half-day.
posts.notes: Drone over three temples + reflection in pool wide + mosaic detail close.

posts.caption: Sunrise kayak from Patara Beach. Paddles in still water, the sky changing colour every minute, only the gulls awake before you. Two-hour trip, back in time for breakfast.
posts.cta: DM us to join the next sunrise group.
posts.notes: Pre-dawn launch, paddle close-up, horizon dawn timelapse.

posts.caption: Tlos — Bellerophon's home in mythology, a hilltop city in geography. Rock-cut tombs in the cliff face, an acropolis with one of the best views in Lycia, a Roman stadium where games were held until the 6th century.
posts.cta: Save — combine with Saklıkent Canyon (15 min away).
posts.notes: 7-slide carousel: cover + tombs + acropolis + theatre + stadium + Bellerophon legend + practical info.

posts.caption: Kalkan after midnight. A meyhane table, an ud, a saz, and a long story no one wants to interrupt. Friday nights work like this here.
posts.cta: DM Friday reservations — tables fill by 21:00.
posts.notes: Wide table shot, musician close-up, rakı pour, table cheers.

posts.caption: Kaputaş from above. A 195-step staircase down to the most photographed beach in the Mediterranean. Worth every step.
posts.cta: Save — arrive before 11:00 for parking.
posts.notes: Slow rotating drone + horizontal pan + final aerial pull-out.

posts.caption: Pinara — a city carved into a cliff face. Hundreds of rock tombs, an acropolis at the top, a city that stayed hidden in plain sight for centuries. The drone shots only hint at the scale.
posts.cta: Save — best light is golden hour, 18:30-19:30.
posts.notes: Cliff tombs reveal 0-10s, acropolis 10-25s, golden hour pull-back 25-45s.

posts.caption: Three days in Kalkan, one perfect order. Day 1 — Patara at sunrise, Xanthos for lunch, dinner on the harbour. Day 2 — Blue Cave boat day, beach club by 4pm, meyhane by 9. Day 3 — Lycian Way morning walk, Kaputaş swim, Pinara golden hour. Save it.
posts.cta: Save — every link is in our bio.

posts.caption: Saklıkent Canyon. Eighteen kilometres long, walls 300 metres high, an ice-cold stream you walk through up to your knees. The first 4 km are open to visitors — that's enough to feel small.
posts.cta: DM for the best half-day combo (Tlos + Saklıkent).
posts.notes: POV walk through water, wide canyon shot, light beam from above.

posts.caption: Patara — 18 kilometres of sand and a single line of footprints in front of you. The loggerhead turtles nest here from May to October — that's why the beach closes at sundown.
posts.cta: Save — visit before 18:00 for the turtles.
posts.notes: Long horizontal pan, footprint close-up, conservation sign frame.

posts.caption: Kekova — the sunken city. Two thousand years ago an earthquake dropped the harbour into the sea. The walls are still there, under three metres of clear water. Glass-bottom boats leave Üçağız every hour.
posts.cta: Save — half-day tour from Kalkan is 4 hours.
posts.notes: Boat bow 0-5s, underwater wall reveal 5-20s, drone of Kaleköy fortress 20-35s.
